newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger chooses new parliament on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Niger chooses new parliament on Saturday.

text.p: Voters in the West African country of Niger choose a new national assembly on Saturday with the main opposition boycotting the poll, accusing President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara of rigging his own election in July.

But an attempt by established opposition politicians, including Mahamane Ousmane the elected civilian Mainassara ousted in January, to close down the nation's towns on Friday fell flat, with the public and private sector working normally.

Mainassara, in a message to the nation when campaigning closed on Thursday, said no-one had the right to hold the nation hostage. "It is urgent to turn our back on internal quarrels, intolerance and brain-washing to apply ourselves to building the nation," he said.
Polls open on Saturday at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) and close at 7 p.m. (1800 GMT).
A total of 220 candidates from around a dozen parties are running, including the Union of Independents for Democratic Renewal which supports Mainassara.
Around 3.8 million people are eligible to vote at more than 8,300 polling stations across the vast and poverty-stricken nation. Niger has closed its borders for the poll.
Politicians ousted by Mainassara have refused to register, demanding that results of July's presidential election be scrapped.

On July 8, the second day of chaotic polling, Mainassara suspended the electoral commission and placed his opponents under house arrest. He appointed a new commission which declared him elected with 52.22 percent of votes cast.
The United States said the election was fraudulent and suspended development aid. It has warned its nationals here to take security precautions on Saturday.
"The possibility exists that campaign activities and demonstrations could turn unruly and result in some form of civil unrest," the U.S. Embassy in Niamey said.
Like many of its neighbours in Sub-Saharan Africa, mainly Moslem Niger launched democratic reforms in the 1990s after the collapse of Communist rule in the Soviet Union.

It held presidential and parliamentary elections in 1993 but government became paralysed by squabbling between Mahamane and his prime minister Amadou Hama who was from a rival group which gained a majority in the 83-seat parliament.
Early parliamentary elections in January 1995 failed to resolve the standoff and Mainassara seized power a year later, drawing widespread international criticism.

After his July election, Mainassara tried to persuade the opposition, which is grouped within the Front for the Restoration and Defence of Democracy, to take part in the parliamentary poll. Negotiations collapsed with the opposition also demanding reinstatement of the old electoral commission.

Mainassara accused that commission of irregularities. A new electoral commission has been set up for the parliamentary poll with members drawn from representatives of all those parties who have signed up for the elections.
Provisional results, which have to be verified by the Supreme Court, could be known within 48 hours of polls closing.
